textPlacement.assessment: Both contexts let book length and handling follow interest while preserving repeated reading, adult enjoyment and the book’s flexible treatment of pretend stories.
Sounds and gestures remain valid conversation in both ages, with silence, unhurried replies and culturally qualified eye contact preserved.
The new contexts distinguish familiar exploration from the later pretend-play discussion, while existing favorites remain sufficient and school materials need not be duplicated.
Both contexts keep multilingual arrangements tied to the family’s actual people and routines, with alternatives and the absence of a fluency timetable preserved.
Shared enjoyment, responding to the child and listening remain sufficient participation without musical skill or performance expectations.
The age variants preserve exploration before matching, identical before similar pictures and no naming test within either browse band.
Both contexts invite small discoveries without a lesson or required outing, while time and alternatives for families without outdoor space remain visible.
The age variants keep the child’s chosen movement central and do not make the equipment list or its differing readiness conditions a set of achievements.
The new contexts preserve an attributed Montessori perspective and family anecdote, with practical alternatives and connection rather than guilt or promised outcomes.
The contexts preserve interest-led choices, shared return and adult modeling without requiring a rotation schedule or a complete work cycle.
Both ages retain genuinely inaccessible small parts, personal space and adaptable arrangements without turning privacy into exclusion during distress.
